transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording ID: fireflies-20260305-zenith-001
Attendees: Marissa Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Anika Bose (Redwood Solutions), Priya Patel (Zenith Partnerships), Liam O'Connor (Zenith Platform Eng), Sam Wong (Zenith Security), Nora Li (Zenith Product)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing artifacts, reference architecture for Redwood Private / Dedicated options, and a joint solution packaging for Zenith's managed data platform. Main goals: decide integration points, security gating items (KMS, SSO, audit logs), and plan a short benchmark to validate latency/cost.

Topics:
- Marketplace tile content and listing process
- Reference architecture (VPC, peering, Private deployment vs Dedicated)
- Auth and key management (SAML, SSO, KMS/HSM)
- Benchmarks and test payloads
- Joint solution GTM artifacts and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Marissa: ok everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off. This is marissa from Redwood, with diego and anika. you folks from zenith?
[00:08] Priya: yeah thanks marissa, priya here. super excited to get this moving, we had initial go/no-go with partnerships, want to understand listing requirements and the technical bits.
[00:16] Diego: great, i'll focus on the infra and e2e integration items. first question, are you planning to list a hosted integration only or are you aiming for a full reference architecture + managed joint solution?
[00:28] Nora: ideally both — marketplace tile first, then a reference arch for customers who want a managed Zenith + Redwood private deployment. also interested in a joint solution badge.
[00:37] Marissa: makes sense. we typically do a marketplace tile with descriptions, screenshots, install guide, and then a reference-arch doc that shows networking, terraform, and recommended sizing. the joint solution is a go-to-market doc that marketing teams co-sign.
[00:47] Liam: quick detail on "private deployment" — is that your VPC-hosted private control plane or the on-prem package?
[00:53] Diego: so two paths: Redwood Private can run in your VPC with our control plane or an on-prem bundle for air-gapped. for marketplace customers, we usually recommend VPC/private control plane unless they require air-gap. the dedicated capacity product is separate — reserved GPU pools for high throughput.
[01:10] Sam: security question: what KMS integrations do you support? we need to ensure envelope encryption, and our compliance folks insist on HSM-backed keys for certain workloads.
[01:20] Diego: we support cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and have a path for HSM integration for Private—some additional ops work will be required. our team also logs token-level audit logs, but i should call out that the audit export format might be slightly different between hosted and private.
[01:35] Priya: that's fine, can you share a sample of the audit log format? our security team will want to map fields.
[01:40] Diego: yes i'll attach a sample; marissa will send the pack after.
[01:44] Marissa: yep will send. also we have a marketplace checklist that covers tile copy, hero screenshot, support contacts, pricing model, and required legal metadata.
[01:54] Priya: on pricing — do you allow listing of both usage-based (hosted) and quoted dedicated bundles?
[01:59] Marissa: yes, tile can indicate hosted pricing tiers; for dedicated or private we usually do a contact-sales CTA that links to a quote flow.
[02:06] Nora: for the reference arch, we want recommended terraform modules so our customers can deploy the integrated stack. do you provide example modules?
[02:14] Diego: we have sample terraform snippets for VPC peering, IAM roles, and service account setup. i'll draft a snippet but you may need to adapt for zenith's infra.
[02:21] Liam: perfect. about peering — any constraints on IP ranges? we have existing corporate ranges that we can't change.
[02:27] Diego: typical approach is to request your CIDR ranges; we suggest non-overlapping space. we also support transit or private-link style setups if peering isn't possible.
[02:36] Priya: ok action — we'll provide CIDR and expected concurrency.
[02:40] Sam: regarding auth, we use SAML SSO, and also want row-level RBAC between tenants. how does Redwood handle multi-tenant RBAC for the console and APIs?
[02:50] Diego: Redwood has RBAC that can map to your SAML groups; for Private we can integrate with your IdP and sync group membership. Some of the finer-grained tenant isolation patterns will need config — i'll outline options in a doc.
[03:03] Marissa: also want to call out model and quantization choices for cost — if you're packaging a joint solution, we can recommend quantized variants for dedicated nodes to reduce cost per token.
[03:15] Nora: that sounds useful — can you share examples and expected cost delta?
[03:18] Diego: yes i'll share a small table; note the numbers are workload-dependent but we have profiling runs we can share.
[03:25] Marissa: next up, how do we handle verifications and tests for the marketplace? we usually ask partners to run a smoke test with a sample prompt set and share latency/throughput numbers.
[03:35] Priya: we can do that — liam can produce load profiles.
[03:38] Liam: yep i'll produce a 1k user simulated profile, with mix: 70% short queries, 20% mid, 10% long. target p95 under 150ms for short queries.
[03:47] Diego: that target is achievable on dedicated with proper batching; on hosted it depends on tenant routing and cached prefixes. we'll run the benchmark both against hosted and a dedicated config if you're evaluating both.
[03:58] Sam: on compliance docs, do you have a pack for SOC2, ISO, pen test summaries?
[04:03] Marissa: yes we have a security pack; marissa: i'll send it along. it includes SOC2 attest, encryption in transit and at rest summary, and standard pen test top-line.
[04:12] Sam: great. also need to confirm data retention options and whether logs can be pushed to our SIEM.
[04:18] Diego: logs can be streamed to your SIEM; for Private deployments logs can remain in your cloud account and we can provide S3 export connectors.
[04:25] Nora: for joint solution messaging, marketing will want a short architecture diagram and a one-page value prop. can redwood provide a reference diagram we can co-brand?
[04:35] Marissa: yes we can supply a template. we also offer a "reference arch" PDF that shows network flows, components (Redwood inference tier, KV cache, prefetch), and recommended sizing.
[04:47] Priya: how long between us sharing info and having a listing live?
[04:51] Marissa: once we have tile assets, security pack, and the smoke test results, marketplace listing can go live in 2-3 weeks typically. longer if legal review stalls.
[04:59] Priya: legal might need the MSA redlined; is there a standard partner MSA?
[05:04] Marissa: we have a partner addendum; for enterprise private deployments there may be an SOW; legal reviews usually 1-2 weeks.
[05:12] -- 10 minute mark noise/side conversation --
[05:34] Diego: quick technical question — do you plan to surface Redwood's cost controls in the tile or documentation? e.g. batching, KV cache, quant profiles that reduce unit cost?
[05:45] Nora: yes that's a selling point for us — customers care about predictable costs. we'd like an example config showing cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:53] Diego: we'll include a sample config and guidance, maybe a small table: batching windows, qps, and expected cost per 1k tokens.
[06:02] Marissa: ok pulling items together: i'll send the marketplace checklist and security pack; diego sends terraform snippets and a sample audit log; priya/l and team send CIDR and traffic profiles.
[06:12] Priya: sounds good. one more question — certification or "verified" badges on the marketplace? any criteria?
[06:18] Marissa: we have a "Redwood Verified" partner badge for integrations that pass both security and performance criteria; criteria include SOC2, successful smoke test, and documented reference arch. we'll share the badge requirements.
[06:28] Sam: on HSM, some customers require FIPS 140-2 validated modules; do you support that for key wrap?
[06:34] Diego: we can integrate with HSM-backed KMS but there are operational steps; we'll list out options and the expected work.
[06:42] Liam: can we run a short perf run with a small model (e.g. 7B) to estimate cost and latency?
[06:48] Diego: yes we'll run a 7B quantized scenario; prefer you send a few representative prompts and sample traffic.
[06:55] Priya: action: we'll produce prompts and traffic; liam will own.
[07:00] Marissa: final recap then next steps:
[07:04] Marissa: Redwood deliverables: marketplace checklist + sample tile, security pack (SOC2 + audit examples), terraform snippets for VPC/peering and IAM, sample audit log format, a short cost/latency table for 7B quantized and dedicated sizing.
[07:18] Marissa: Zenith deliverables: CIDR ranges, expected concurrency/traffic profile, sample prompts, security requirements for KMS/HSM, and point of contact for legal.
[07:30] Priya: we'll aim to have those by the dates discussed.
[07:33] Nora: thanks all — excited to move forward.
[07:36] Marissa: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench and reference arch review.

End of recording.
